en: publish; run; print (an article, ad or photo)

examples.en: The newspaper published a reader's piece.
I'll post the notice on our website.
You need permission if you want to publish a photo.

examples.ko: 잡지에 광고를 게재하는 데 비용이 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to run an ad in a magazine?
The editor printed my story for me.

examples.ko: 오류가 있어서 기사를 다시 게재하기로 했어요.
examples.en: There was an error, so we decided to run the article again.

explain: 게재하다는 글, 광고, 사진을 신문이나 인터넷에 싣는 일에 써서 공지, 기사, 광고 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 말할 때는 인터넷이면 '올리다', 신문·잡지면 '싣다'를 더 많이 써요. 보통 '~에 ~을/를 게재하다'로 써요.
explain_en: 게재하다 is used for putting an article, ad or photo in a newspaper or online, so it appears mostly around notices, news and ads. In speech people say 올리다 for online and 싣다 for print. The usual pattern is ~에 ~을/를 게재하다.

examples.en: The company officially disclosed this year's results.
City Hall posts the new rules officially on its website.
The bank will publicly announce its interest rates every month.
The date for publicly announcing the results has been set.
That information hasn't been officially disclosed yet.

examples.ko: 법에 따라 회사는 중요한 내용을 공시해야 해요.
examples.en: By law, a company has to disclose important information publicly.

explain: '발표하다'는 누구나 쓰지만 '공시하다'는 회사나 관청이 규칙에 따라 공식적으로 알릴 때 써요. 경제 뉴스나 기업 보고서에서 많이 보고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: 발표하다 works for anyone, but 공시하다 is for a company or government office announcing something officially, following rules. You see it in business news and reports, almost never in daily conversation.

examples.en: The school announced the vacation schedule.
I posted a notice at the shop that we're closed tomorrow.
I'll announce important things in the group chat.

examples.ko: 변경된 시간을 공지하지 않아서 혼란이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because the changed time wasn't announced, confusion arose.

examples.ko: 회사가 이메일로 새 규칙을 공지하는 중이에요.
examples.en: The company is announcing the new rule by email.
As announced, class starts at 7.

explain: '공지하다'는 학교, 회사, 가게가 여러 사람에게 정해진 내용을 알릴 때 써요. 친구에게 개인적으로 알릴 때는 '알려 주다'를 써요. 명사 '공지'는 앱이나 홈페이지의 '공지사항'에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: 공지하다 is used when a school, company or shop informs many people of a fixed matter. For telling a friend personally, use 알려 주다. The noun 공지 appears often as 공지사항 (notices) in apps and websites.

dis.h: notify members or staff of an update

p.n: 공지 is a notice to people in the group; 공고 is a public posting open to everyone.

examples.en: A notice recruiting employees has been posted on the bulletin board.
Election posters are plastered in every alley.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 학교 벽에 나붙자 학생들이 몰려들었어요.
examples.en: When the exam results went up on the school wall, students crowded around.

examples.ko: 가게 문에 휴업 안내문이 나붙었는데 못 봤어요?
examples.en: A notice of closure was put up on the shop door; didn't you see it?

examples.ko: 새 규칙이 나붙으면 꼭 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: When a new rule is posted, be sure to read it.

examples.ko: 건물 벽에 광고가 마구 나붙는 게 문제예요.
examples.en: The problem is that ads are being stuck up all over the building walls.

explain: 그냥 '붙다'와 달리 사람들이 볼 수 있게 공고문, 포스터, 방 같은 것이 눈에 띄는 곳에 붙을 때 써요. 스스로 붙는 게 아니라 누가 붙여 놓은 것이 보이는 상황이에요. 붙이는 사람을 말할 때는 '붙이다'를 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '붙다', it is used when a notice, poster or announcement is put up in a place where everyone can see it. The focus is on the visible result of someone having posted it. When you name the person who put it up, use '붙이다'.

examples.en: Participants are recruited this week.
A hundred volunteers were recruited.
I'll contact you as soon as staff are recruited.

examples.ko: 학생이 충분히 모집되지 않아서 수업이 취소됐어요.
examples.en: The class was canceled because not enough students signed up.
The people who were recruited will gather next week.
New members will soon be recruited.

explain: '모집되다'는 사람을 구하는 일이 진행되어 사람들이 모였을 때 써요. 구하는 쪽은 '모집하다'를 써요. 공고에서는 '모집 중'이나 '모집 마감'처럼 짧게 자주 써요.
explain_en: 모집되다 is used when a drive to find people has progressed and people have been gathered. The side doing the recruiting uses 모집하다. In notices you often see the short forms 모집 중 (now recruiting) and 모집 마감 (recruitment closed).

dis.h: called for or gathered, like members

p.n: 채용되다 means actually hired; 모집되다 means applicants are being sought.

examples.en: The book I ordered was shipped yesterday.
The email is sent automatically at the set time.
The invitations were sent out to all the guests.
I will let you know by text when the item is shipped.

examples.ko: 아직 발송되지 않은 편지가 책상에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a letter on the desk that has not been sent yet.

examples.ko: 발송된 소포는 이틀 뒤에 도착할 거예요.
examples.en: The parcel that was sent will arrive in two days.

explain: 발송되다는 쇼핑몰 문자나 회사 안내에서 자주 보는 '보내졌다'의 공식적인 말이에요. 주어는 물건·메일·서류예요. 내가 보낼 때는 '보내다'를 쓰고, 회사가 보낼 때 '발송하다'를 써요.
explain_en: 발송되다 is the formal 'has been sent' that you see in shopping-site texts and company notices; the subject is an item, mail or document. When you send something yourself you say '보내다'; a company says '발송하다'.

examples.en: This magazine is published every month.

examples.ko: 새 책이 다음 주에 발행될 거예요.
examples.en: The new book will be published next week.

examples.ko: 표는 결제한 뒤에 바로 발행되고 있어요.
examples.en: Tickets are issued right after payment.
I read a newspaper that was published long ago.
So far one million copies have been printed.

examples.ko: 기념 우표가 발행되면 우체국에 줄이 길어요.
examples.en: When a commemorative stamp is issued, the line at the post office gets long.

explain: 책, 신문, 잡지, 영수증, 표, 우표 모두 '발행되다'와 쓸 수 있어요. 책은 '출판되다', '출간되다'도 쓰는데, 영수증이나 표처럼 만들어 내주는 것에는 '발행되다'가 어울려요.
explain_en: Books, newspapers, magazines, receipts, tickets, and stamps can all be '발행되다'. Books also use '출판되다' and '출간되다', but for things that are produced and handed out, like receipts and tickets, '발행되다' fits.

p.n: 출판되다 is for books or printed works, not stamps.

examples.en: The notice was handed out to all students.
The new version will be released tomorrow.
Masks are being handed out for free.
I'll tell you by email once the materials are out.
A wrong file got released, and now we're in trouble.
Please update the released app now.

explain: 배포하다의 피동이에요. 누가 나눠 줬는지보다 나눠졌다는 사실이 중요할 때 써요. 공지, 뉴스, 앱 업데이트 소식에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is the passive of '배포하다'. Use it when the fact that something went out matters more than who sent it. It shows up often in notices, news, and app update announcements.

en: meeting to launch the New Year

examples.ko: 연초 시무식에는 임직원이 모두 대강당에 모여요.
examples.en: At the New Year launch ceremony, all the staff gather in the main hall.
This year's opening ceremony is held on the morning of January 2.
At the opening ceremony, the CEO announced this year's goals.
Our company keeps the New Year opening ceremony simple.
After the opening ceremony, I ate rice cake soup with my teammates.

examples.ko: 시무식 때 입을 정장을 미리 챙겨 놓았어요.
examples.en: I got my suit ready in advance for the opening ceremony.

explain: 회사나 기관에서 새해 첫 출근일에 하는 행사예요. 반대로 한 해를 마무리하는 행사는 '종무식'이라고 해요. '시무식을 하다', '시무식을 열다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is the event a company or organization holds on the first working day of the new year. The event that wraps up the year is called '종무식'. You say '시무식을 하다' or '시무식을 열다'.

examples.en: Submission of this document is requested by tomorrow.
If help is requested, I'll go right away.
Attendance at the meeting was requested.
It's a situation where cooperation is requested.
Additional materials may be requested.

examples.ko: 요청된 일은 오늘 안에 끝내야 해요.
examples.en: The requested work has to be finished today.

explain: '~이/가 요청되다'는 주어가 요청받는 일이라서 누가 요청했는지는 말하지 않아요. 안내문, 공문, 뉴스에서 자주 보이고 일상 대화에서는 '부탁받다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the thing being asked for, and who asked is left unsaid. You see it in notices, official letters, and news. In everyday talk people prefer simpler phrasing such as 부탁받다.

dis.h: be asked for politely; formally requested

p.n: 요구되다 makes it sound like a demand or requirement, not a polite request.

examples.en: The president is in his office right now.
I waited for a moment in front of the office door.
The mayor's office is on the third floor.
The office was full of a big desk and papers.
When guests come, we talk in the office.
The president's office appeared on the news.

explain: 집무실은 높은 직책의 사람이 일하는 방이에요. 일반 직원의 일하는 곳은 '사무실'이라고 하고, 사장이나 시장처럼 책임이 큰 사람의 방일 때 집무실이라고 해요. 보통 '대통령 집무실', '사장 집무실'처럼 직책과 함께 말해요.
explain_en: 집무실 is the room where a high-ranking person works. A regular employee's workplace is a 사무실, while 집무실 is used for the room of someone with big responsibility, like a president or mayor. It usually comes with a title, as in 대통령 집무실 or 사장 집무실.

en: first issue; launch of a publication

examples.ko: 이 잡지는 올해 창간 오십 주년을 맞았어요.
examples.en: This magazine marks the fiftieth anniversary of its launch this year.

examples.ko: 신문사는 창간 기념 행사를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: The newspaper company is preparing an event to celebrate its founding.
The first issue sold out in a few days.

examples.ko: 그 잡지의 창간 멤버들이 오랜만에 모였어요.
examples.en: The founding members of the magazine got together for the first time in a long while.

examples.ko: 창간 때부터 이 칼럼을 읽어 왔어요.
examples.en: I have been reading this column since the very first issue.

examples.ko: 창간 준비 중인 웹진에서 글을 부탁했어요.
examples.en: A webzine that is getting ready to launch asked me to write something.

explain: 창간은 신문이나 잡지를 처음 낼 때 써요. 방송이 처음 시작할 때는 '개국', 가게는 '개업'처럼 분야마다 말이 달라요. 반대로 신문이나 잡지를 아예 접을 때는 '폐간'이라고 해요.
explain_en: This word is only for the very first issue of a newspaper or magazine. Other fields have their own words: a broadcaster starting up is '개국' and a shop opening is '개업'. Shutting a publication down for good is '폐간'.

examples.en: A new menu item was added.
The name wasn't added to the list.
If you order, a shipping fee is added.
A new feature will be added to the app.
I marked the added content in yellow.
One more assignment got added, so it's tough.

explain: 이미 있는 것에 더해진다는 말이에요. 반대로 빠지는 것은 '삭제되다', '제외되다'를 써요. 직접 더할 때는 '추가하다'예요. 돈이 더 붙을 때는 '비용이 추가되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means something is added on top of what already exists. The opposite, for things taken out, is '삭제되다' or '제외되다'. When you add something yourself, use '추가하다'. Extra costs are also described with this verb: '비용이 추가되다'.
